Mongo: build Document and Query filters from typed BSON values

commits.author: Marco Pagan
commits.message:
Mongo: build Document and Query filters from typed BSON values

Filter values were rendered to JSON text and parsed back with Document.parse,
so dates ended up as strings and comparisons against date fields returned
wrong results. Document and Query parameters, and the new FilterQueryConverter,
are now built directly from BSON values: dates, ObjectIds, UUIDs and numbers
keep their type. ObjectNode parameters keep using the JSON transformer.

Also fixes placeholder processor injection, resolves ObjectId fields like
String ids, and drops the application.properties shipped in the jar.

Merge pull request #521 from marcopag90/remove-jackson2

Migrate mongo module from Jackson 2 to Jackson 3

commits.author: Marco Pagan
commits.message:
Migrate mongo module from Jackson 2 to Jackson 3

The mongo module was the last one compiling against Jackson 2
(com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind). Move it to Jackson 3
(tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind, managed by the Spring Boot 4 BOM)
so that no springfilter module declares or imports Jackson 2 anymore.

Changes:
- mongo/pom.xml: swap jackson-databind groupId to tools.jackson.core
- Swap com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.* imports to tools.jackson.databind.*
  across the transformer, helper, argument resolver and all 22 processors
- Rename textNode()/asText() to stringNode()/asString() (TextNode is
  StringNode in Jackson 3, and the old aliases are deprecated)
- Create value nodes through getNodeFactory() instead of the previous
  createObjectNode().textNode(...) idiom, which allocated a throwaway
  ObjectNode per call just to reach the factory method
- Tests: provide the mapper bean via JsonMapper.builder().build() and drop
  the try/catch around readTree(), which now throws unchecked
  JacksonException instead of IOException

This also fixes a latent DI mismatch: the auto-configured beans injected a
Jackson 2 ObjectMapper, but Spring Boot 4 only auto-configures the Jackson 3
JsonMapper, so the mongo auto-configuration could not start on a default
Boot 4 context.

Jackson annotations (com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.*) are intentionally
untouched: Jackson 3 keeps using that package. The Jackson 2 jars still
reachable transitively through springdoc/swagger-core in the example modules
stay until swagger-core ships a Jackson 3 line.
